title: Migration from CUCM, UCCX, and UCCE
blurb: Migration Insights, feature CSVs, the park and pickup gap, and why contact center scripts are a redesign.

lessons.title: Start with Migration Insights
lessons.summary: Cisco's prepare article points you at Control Hub Migration Insights. Upload the Unified CM tar. CDR is optional, and it is required if you want the feature-usage reports.
objectives: Separate tar reports from CDR reports
Keep PSTN choices to one per location

diagram.caption: Tar for configuration. CDR for usage. Both are exports, not a cutover.

steps.label: Open Migration Insights
steps.detail: The prepare article recommends starting there. Import the Unified CM export tar and, if you want usage, the CDR files.
steps.inspect: Services path as the live Hub shows

steps.label: Read the configuration CSVs
steps.detail: ImportedDataBulk.csv, DeviceEligibility.csv, device-pool numbers, the shared-feature group file, hunt insight, and the shared-line report are the tar table.
steps.inspect: No calls required

steps.label: Read usage only if you uploaded it
steps.detail: Feature-usage eligibility, hunt and queue usage with last date, user and workspace last usage, and DID usage need the CDR gzip files.
steps.inspect: Optional means the upload, not the insight

steps.label: One PSTN option per location
steps.detail: The same article says a Control Hub location is assigned to one PSTN option: Cisco Calling Plan, Cloud Connected PSTN, or premises local gateway.
steps.inspect: Choose before you move users

sections.h: The tar table and the CDR table
paragraphs: Tar reports describe users, devices, eligibility, device pools, hunt and pickup grouping, hunt lines, and shared lines.
CDR reports describe usage. Uploading a tar alone will not produce last-usage dates.

cite.label: Migration Insights

paragraphs: The prepare article lists people who share lines, hunt pilots, pickup groups, call park numbers, intercom, and admin/exec relationships. The group CSV is how Insights shows that.
Splitting a shared line across two weekends is how Monday morning breaks.

lessons.title: Call queues and auto attendants
lessons.summary: Migrate features writes CallQueueBulk.csv and Auto-AttendantBulk.csv. Both can contain errors. Remove the Errors and Notes columns before you upload to Control Hub.
objectives: Use the generated CSV, not a blank one
Upload queues and auto attendants in their own tools

lessons.title: Park and pickup need the script
lessons.summary: The migrate-features tool does not create call park and call pickup files. The Python script UserBasedUCMFeatureMigration does. It also filters by a user list.
objectives: List the other files it writes

diagram.caption: The gap is documented. The script is the documented fill.

steps.label: Notice park and pickup are missing
steps.detail: The article says the script creates CallPark.csv and CallPickupgroup.csv because the migrate-features tool does not currently support them.
steps.inspect: Do not hand-build from rumor

steps.label: Point it at the CDR export
steps.detail: The script processes CDR collected on a server or Unified CM. The compressed result can be uploaded in Control Hub.
steps.inspect: Follow the migration utility script page

steps.label: Pass a user list
steps.detail: It can filter the main tool's output by users and override locations with a Location column.
steps.inspect: People outside the list but in a group are identified

steps.label: Read DNInMultipleDevicePool.csv
steps.detail: Directory numbers in more than one device pool are listed under insightDir.
steps.inspect: Resolve them before cutover

sections.h: What the script will not invent
paragraphs: It does not convert UCCX scripts. It is a Webex Calling feature helper.
Call park extensions also appear as CallParkExtensionBulk.csv from the main tool. Read both pages before you decide which file you are uploading.

sections.h: Dedicated Instance still has Unity Connection
paragraphs: If the design is Dedicated Instance, Unity Connection is deployed as part of that add-on. That is not the multi-tenant Webex Calling voicemail path this lesson is about.
Do not tell a DI customer that their messages cannot exist, and do not tell a multi-tenant customer that Unity will be connected.

lessons.title: UCCX and UCCE are a redesign
